title: Eleven Minutes of Swinging
subtitle: 山川山地 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 山川山地（自然生态·山川与地形）
meta: 主题语境：山川山地（自然生态·山川与地形）　|　核心词汇：compass　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 compass 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 my uncle ① took a compass up a mountain that had no path, and he said the taking was the whole of the climb. The ② compass, meaning the needle and not the map, swung for eleven minutes and stayed that way; compass, he said, is the only thing on a mountain that is judged by how little it is trusted.

Every ③ compass in that pack had the same scratch, and the ④ compass at the end, meaning the one he kept for the descent and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever checked twice. Compass, my aunt said, is nine parts checking and one part somebody willing to trust it; my uncle said the checking is the part that fills the descent.

My grandmother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ a compass was the whole of the geometry lesson, meaning the pair of legs and not the needle. The ⑥ compass, meaning the pair of legs and not any of that, is the only thing in a lesson that everybody borrows and nobody owns; compass, she said, is either something you take up a mountain or the only word that means both a needle and a pair of legs. He said the legs are the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ compass had become a line in an inventory, and the inventory had become an argument about the scratch. The ⑧ compass of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in September, was one needle and thirty years of checking; compass, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to trust it. She said the trusting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ compass I remember is the one at the end, which he took up in 1966 and is still described as the most scratched in the county. A ⑩ compass, my aunt said in 1968, is the only thing that improves by being checked; every compass, she said, is a direction that has agreed to look like a needle. She said the direction was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 指南针（指那枚指针本身，与那张地图相对）

answers.why: take a compass 意为“带上指南针”，1952 年叔叔带了一枚指南针上一座没有路的山。
compass 意为“指南针”，指那枚指针本身而不是那张地图，它摆动了十一分钟。
compass 指那只背包里每一枚指南针，每一枚都有同样的划痕。
compass 指末尾那一枚（他留给下山用的那一枚），是唯一有人核对过两次的。
compass 意为“圆规”，祖母说圆规就是那堂几何课的全部，指的是那两条腿而不是那枚指针。
compass 为另一个义项，指那两条腿而不是那枚指针，是课堂上人人都借、却无人拥有的东西。
compass 意为“指南针”，指清单里提到的那一枚，到 1960 年这枚指南针成了清单里的一行。
compass 意为“方向感、判断”，叔叔九月写道，整件事的方向感是一枚指针三十年的核对。
compass 意为“指南针”，我记得的是末尾那一枚，他 1966 年带上山，至今仍被说成全县划痕最多的。
compass 为抽象总称，姑姑说一枚指南针是唯一会因为被核对而变好的东西。
